content.title: About
content.content: The Italian sandwich on wheat is a classic light lunch consisting of a fresh wheat roll, slices of prosciutto, mozzarella, tomatoes, basil and olive oil. The sandwich combines aromatic Italian ingredients with the soft texture of the bread.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Basil used in the sandwich is considered a symbol of Italy and is often associated with the scent of Mediterranean cuisine.
Prosciutto is a dry‑cured ham traditionally produced in the Parma and San Daniele regions.
Traditional mozzarella is made from water buffalo milk, but most commercial versions use cow’s milk.
A wheat roll provides a softer structure compared with classic ciabatta, making the sandwich easy to eat on the go.
The sandwich is often served with balsamic vinegar or balsamic glaze for extra tang.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Prosciutto and mozzarella supply high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Olive oil contains monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Basil, tomatoes and mozzarella provide vitamin C, vitamin K, calcium and magnesium.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The wheat roll, especially when whole‑grain, adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and basil are rich in lycopene and polyphenols, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Mozzarella may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prosciutto is relatively salty; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The wheat roll contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑dense due to oil and cheese; moderate consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the roll horizontally, brush the interior with olive oil, then layer prosciutto, mozzarella, tomato slices and basil leaves. A drizzle of balsamic vinegar or glaze can be added to taste. The sandwich can be eaten by hand or with a fork and knife.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed fresh. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in plastic film and keep in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Store the roll in a dry place, and keep cheese and ham in separate containers.
